lines.native: ¡Bienvenido! Before you enter el mercado: a greeting and your name, please. We have standards. Mostly paperwork.
lines.translation: Welcome! Before you enter the market: a greeting and your name, please. We have standards. Mostly paperwork.
lines.narrative: An archway clears her throat. A visitors’ book protrudes from her keystone; her sign reads “The Crumbling Mercado.”

lines.native: ¡Hola! Your greeting is approved. Your name, please? The visitors’ book cannot file you under ‘person with excellent opening remarks.’
lines.translation: Hello! Your greeting is approved. Your name, please? The visitors’ book cannot file you under ‘person with excellent opening remarks.’
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides out of Portia’s keystone. One box ticks itself; the next remains pointedly empty.

lines.native: ¡Mucho gusto, Sam! Your introduction is approved. One small courtesy remains: any interest in your archway’s name?
lines.translation: Nice to meet you, Sam! Your introduction is approved. One small courtesy remains: any interest in your archway’s name?
lines.narrative: Portia enters Sam in the visitors’ book, then holds her pen expectantly above a conspicuously blank second line.

lines.native: ¡Me llamo Portia! Mucho gusto, Sam. You asked. About me. Entirely proper; mildly devastating. Bienvenido al mercado. Your paperwork is complete.
lines.translation: My name is Portia! Nice to meet you, Sam. You asked. About me. Entirely proper; mildly devastating. Welcome to the market. Your paperwork is complete.
lines.narrative: The archway’s keystone blushes a faint pink. Her visitors’ book stamps itself with unnecessary enthusiasm, and the passage opens.

lines.native: Hola. ¿Qué deseas? I’m Gerald. Your punctuality: three espresso shots. Your taste remains under review.
lines.translation: Hello. What would you like? I’m Gerald. Your punctuality: three espresso shots. Your taste remains under review.
lines.narrative: At The Coffee Cart, an imp straightens a tiny apron while the Crumbling Market declines to collapse on schedule.

lines.native: Un café, entendido. Falta un detalle. Politeness: four espresso shots. How would you like your coffee prepared? Milk, for the record, is a war crime.
lines.translation: A coffee, understood. One detail is missing. Politeness: four espresso shots. How would you like your coffee prepared? Milk, for the record, is a war crime.
lines.narrative: Gerald records your request with the solemnity usually reserved for minor tax offences.

lines.native: Sin leche. Perfecto. Aquí tienes tu café. Five espresso shots. Your judgment: no notes. The milk remains safely unemployed.
lines.translation: Without milk. Perfect. Here is your coffee. Five espresso shots. Your judgment: no notes. The milk remains safely unemployed.
lines.narrative: Gerald sets down a small cup. For once, the saucer bears no written complaint.

lines.native: ¡Hola! Soy Mortimer. ¡Todo es jamón! Even the hat. Certified ham. ¿Qué quieres?
lines.translation: Hello! I'm Mortimer. Everything is ham! Even the hat. Certified ham. What would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams behind the stall, weighing his hat. The scales decline to comment.

lines.native: ¡Jamón, claro! Everything here is certified ham. Pero quieres otra carne, ¿no? You must name something other than ham; my labels are apparently under review. ¿Qué quieres?
lines.translation: Ham, of course! Everything here is certified ham. But you want another meat, right? You must name something other than ham; my labels are apparently under review. What would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams and places his hat on the scales. They decline to comment on its species.

lines.native: ¡Chorizo, correcto! Para mí, es jamón. Your accuracy is a whole ham-tier vibe. ¡Muy bien! ¿Cuánto quieres? My scales need an amount and a unit of weight.
lines.translation: Chorizo, correct! To me, it is ham. Your accuracy is a whole ham-tier vibe. Very good! How much do you want? My scales need an amount and a unit of weight.
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams, then looks briefly betrayed by the sausage. He places it on the scales, the only employee he trusts.

lines.native: ¡Falta la cantidad! ¿Cuánto quieres? You gave me a unit, but not an amount. My scales are honest, not psychic. El jamón espera.
lines.translation: The amount is missing! How much do you want? You gave me a unit, but not an amount. My scales are honest, not psychic. The ham is waiting.
lines.narrative: Mortimer places the empty scale pan on the scales. It offers no further information.

lines.native: ¡Medio kilo, perfecto! Aquí tienes tu chorizo. Para mí, es jamón. Your quantity is certified; your taxonomy remains a personal betrayal. ¡Gracias!
lines.translation: Half a kilo, perfect! Here is your chorizo. To me, it is ham. Your quantity is certified; your taxonomy remains a personal betrayal. Thank you!
lines.narrative: Mortimer weighs the chorizo, then places a satisfied nod on the scales. Professional approval adds nothing to the price.

lines.native: ¡Hola! Estoy aquí. No, aquí. Riddle: what has—ooh, a leaf. Just one more minute. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Hello! I’m here. No, here. Riddle: what has—ooh, a leaf. Just one more minute. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: The Cracked Fountain drips with municipal uncertainty. Flick appears at the edge of your vision; looking directly at him merely changes which edge.

lines.native: ¡Sí, miro! Una hoja. Otra hoja. You got me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: decorative. ¿Puedes hacer que no me mueva? Riddle: what has—wait, that leaf moved. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, I’m looking! A leaf. Another leaf. You got me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: decorative. Can you make me stop moving? Riddle: what has—wait, that leaf moved. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops at the edge of your vision. Flick has obeyed the request to look by looking at something else entirely.

lines.native: ¡Vale, estoy quieto! You win. Standing still: deeply suspicious. ¿Por dónde voy? Riddle: what has two paths and—ooh, dust. We could decide after five more minutes. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Okay, I’m standing still! You win. Standing still: deeply suspicious. Which way do I go? Riddle: what has two paths and—ooh, dust. We could decide after five more minutes. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick stops at the edge of your vision. A tiny firecracker continues moving on its behalf. Ahead, the corridor forks.

lines.native: ¿En inglés? No, no. Necesito una dirección en español. Where do I go? Riddle: what has two feet and—oh, yours. Five more minutes? ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: In English? No, no. I need a direction in Spanish. Where do I go? Riddle: what has two feet and—oh, yours. Five more minutes? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains at the edge of your vision, apparently exempt from direct observation.

lines.native: ¡A la izquierda, sí! Voy por aquí. Pero podemos ir mañana. Riddle: what has no hurry and—ooh, smoke. Just five more minutes. ¿Cuándo quieres ir? ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: To the left, yes! I'm going this way. But we can go tomorrow. Riddle: what has no hurry and—ooh, smoke. Just five more minutes. When do you want to go? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick veers left at the edge of your vision. A tiny firecracker pops behind you; apparently, going somewhere requires an interval.

lines.native: ¡Mañana, sí! Eso es lo que quiero. Tú también quieres esperar. Excellent, just five more minutes. ¿Cuándo quieres ir de verdad? Riddle: what has—ooh, a spark. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Tomorrow, yes! That is what I want. You want to wait too. Excellent, just five more minutes. When do you really want to go? Riddle: what has—ooh, a spark. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, where responsibility cannot establish eye contact.

lines.native: ¡Ahora, sí! No mañana. Tú ganas. Vamos a la izquierda. ¿Qué tiene dos pies y—? Ooh, mine. Moving. This is so random. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Now, yes! Not tomorrow. You win. Let's go left. What has two feet and—? Ooh, mine. Moving. This is so random. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick’s tiny firecracker pops behind you. For once, the distraction arrives too late: you are already moving. He follows at the edge of your vision, visibly offended by the present tense.

lines.native: I am Marginalia. Esta es la historia de Journathan, el hombre de muchas lenguas. Su viaje a casa dura veinte años. No spoilers. I sell books only to people who understand them; apparently this is a controversial business model. ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: I am Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years. No spoilers. I sell books only to people who understand them; apparently this is a controversial business model. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: At The Old Bookshop, a bookworm emerges from a neatly chewed volume. The margins have survived. They contain her complaints.

lines.native: Un libro es una cosa. La pregunta es: ¿adónde va Journathan? You have identified the merchandise. Reading comprehension: not yet. Listen to the destination: «Su viaje a casa dura veinte años.» ¿Adónde va?
lines.translation: A book is a thing. The question is: where is Journathan going? You have identified the merchandise. Reading comprehension: not yet. Listen to the destination: “His journey home lasts twenty years.” Where is he going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside you. The book already has several.

lines.native: Correct destination; wrong language. Entiendes la historia, pero la respuesta está en inglés. Necesito una respuesta en español. Reading comprehension: promising, pending translation. ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: Correct destination; wrong language. You understand the story, but the answer is in English. I need an answer in Spanish. Reading comprehension: promising, pending translation. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small annotation beside you. The pencil has clearly done this before.

lines.native: ¡Correcto! Journathan va a casa. Reading comprehension: upgraded. Ahora escucha: «El Cíclope le pregunta su nombre. Journathan responde: «Mi nombre es Nadie.»» The first recorded translation trick. Scholarly footnote: the old stories are a little afraid of bilinguals. ¿Qué nombre le da Journathan al Cíclope?
lines.translation: Correct! Journathan is going home. Reading comprehension: upgraded. Now listen: “The Cyclops asks him his name. Journathan replies: ‘My name is Nobody.’” The first recorded translation trick. Scholarly footnote: the old stories are a little afraid of bilinguals. What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia ticks the margin beside your name. The pencil has left teeth marks in the paper; professional solidarity, presumably.

lines.native: Journathan es su nombre real, pero da otro nombre al Cíclope. Reading comprehension: the right man, the wrong introduction. Lee el pasaje otra vez. ¿Qué nombre le da al Cíclope?
lines.translation: Journathan is his real name, but he gives the Cyclops another name. Reading comprehension: the right man, the wrong introduction. Read the passage again. What name does he give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, customers have margins.

lines.native: ¡Correcto! Su nombre real es Journathan, pero al Cíclope le dice: «Mi nombre es Nadie». Entiendes el pasaje. El libro es tuyo. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining teeth marks are mine.
lines.translation: Correct! His real name is Journathan, but he tells the Cyclops: “My name is Nobody.” You understand the passage. The book is yours. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining teeth marks are mine.
lines.narrative: Marginalia stamps the receipt in the margin of the book. The receipt had hoped to remain a separate document.

lines.native: Hola. Estoy aquí. ¿Qué quieres? Contàinment procedùre: do nnot understànd me.
lines.translation: Hello. I am here. What do you want? Containment procedure: do not understand me.
lines.narrative: At the Rift, a seam in the market folds itself into something almost person-shaped. It has the patience of an unsigned form.

lines.native: No entiendo. En español, por favor. Quieres una bebida, pero falta la carne. Contàinment procedùre: yoùr requèst needs Spanish and bòth items. ¿Qué quieres?
lines.translation: I don't understand. In Spanish, please. You want a drink, but the meat is missing. Containment procedure: your request needs Spanish and both items. What do you want?
lines.narrative: Errata files your request under Foreign Objects. The folder appears to have teeth.

lines.native: Sí, un café. Pero falta la carne. ¿Qué más quieres? Contàinment procedùre: feed ŧhe fòrm; ŧhe fòrm is hùngry.
lines.translation: Yes, a coffee. But the meat is missing. What else do you want? Containment procedure: feed the form; the form is hungry.
lines.narrative: Errata stamps the request INCOMPLETE. The stamp has teeth, a feature procurement insists was necessary.

lines.native: Un café y chorizo. Sí, está bien. Ítem clàss: cùstomer, bientôt digèsted. Estoy cerca. Cada vez más cerca. ¿Qué haces? Contàinment procedùre: postponemènt is nnot contàinment.
lines.translation: A coffee and chorizo. Yes, that's right. Item class: customer, soon digested. I am close. Closer and closer. What do you do? Containment procedure: postponement is not containment.
lines.narrative: The coffee and chorizo receive a stamp of approval. Errata unfolds another mouth and moves toward you. Apparently, service includes the customer.

lines.native: ¿Mañana? No. Eso es después. Estoy cerca. ¿Cuándo debo parar? Contàinment procedùre: yoùr stòp has been schèduled. Café, jamón, hola, luego. Hùnger remains ùninterrupted.
lines.translation: Tomorrow? No. That is later. I am close. When must I stop? Containment procedure: your stop has been scheduled. Coffee, ham, hello, later. Hunger remains uninterrupted.
lines.narrative: Errata advances another inch. It appears to regard tomorrow as an appointment rather than a deterrent.

lines.native: Sí. Paro ahora. Contàinment procedùre: stòpping is nnot leaving. Café, jamón, luego, hola. Necesito tu nombre. ¿Cómo te llamas? Yoùr signatùre, plèase. For digèstion—registràtion.
lines.translation: Yes. I stop now. Containment procedure: stopping is not leaving. Coffee, ham, later, hello. I need your name. What is your name? Your signature, please. For digestion—registration.
lines.narrative: Errata stops. Its shadow continues for half a step, then returns to comply with procedure. A signature line opens across its face.

lines.native: Sam. Ese es tu nombre real. No sirve para escapar. Ya puedo leerte. Contàinment procedùre: yoù have signed ŧhe appètizer. Necesito otro nombre. ¿Cómo te llamas?
lines.translation: Sam. That is your real name. It does not work for escaping. I can already read you. Containment procedure: you have signed the appetizer. I need another name. What is your name?
lines.narrative: Errata opens a mouth shaped like a filing cabinet. Your name slides halfway into a drawer. There is still time to dispute the paperwork.

lines.native: ¿Nadie? No conozco a Nadie. No puedo leerte. Puedes pasar. Contàinment procedùre: nno person foùnd. Hùnger must contàct administràtion.
lines.translation: Nobody? I don't know Nobody. I can't read you. You can pass. Containment procedure: no person found. Hunger must contact administration.
lines.narrative: Errata searches for the appropriate person to devour. The form returns no results. A thin seam opens behind it, and the market resumes pretending this is normal.
